_about: Hard rules that jev-rules.py checks before every edit or commit. 'on' is 'edit' or 'commit'. 'paths' (edit rules only) is a regex on the edited file's path relative to the project root; omit it to apply to every file. 'source' is where the rule came from; it's quoted when an edit is blocked. Keep the wording close to the source. These are examples: replace them with your own rules from CLAUDE.md or your specs.

rules.rule: Never hardcode secrets: no API keys, tokens, passwords or private keys in source files. Read them from environment variables.
Frontend code never talks to the database directly (no database clients, SQL, or direct table reads or writes from the browser). All data goes through the backend API.
Every endpoint that reads or changes user data checks on the server that the caller is allowed to, and never trusts a user ID or role sent by the client.
No secrets may be committed: no .env files, no real API keys, passwords or service keys. .env.example files hold placeholders only.
